title: Hustlers Saloon, Chicago Royal Garden, Tick Top and who played there
summary: Locations and atmosphere of Hustlers Saloon, Chicago Royal Garden, Pelican and Tick Top, with Armstrong, Peter William and Guy E playing there.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: How about the Hustlers Saloon on either Rampart or Dryads and Perdido?

It's Rampart and Perdido, where the Hustlers Saloon was. That was on Perdido and Rampart. He used to call it Ben Mulligan too. Ben Mulligan. He was the manager of that bar on there. But he used to call it the Hustlers, the Hustlers Bar. That's right.
A lot of sporting people hanging out there?

Oh, yeah. Women used to come in there. Women used to come in there. And look at a man and say, oh honey, I like you. You say, oh but you're fine. And then they say, how about buying me a drink? Hold on a minute. Hold on a minute.
The Top. He used to call it the Tick Top.

Then they had another place they called Chicago Royal Garden. That is on, Chicago Royal Garden was on, I tell you what it was, it was on, on Gravy. Gravy and Rampart, upstairs, right near the corner. Was that near the Chicago Hotel? No, no. They called it the Chicago Royal Garden. They used to have a band, dancing up there. And they had Pelican. You know about the Pelican place in Tote Island. That was a very popular place too, at that time. And they had the Tick Top. See that story used to be the Tick Top place. It went from a Tick Top to the Golden Dragon. From a Tick Top to Golden Dragon, Golden Dragon to the, that's what they called it now. But it was first a Tick Top. That's the time to roll it.
Do you remember what bands played in there?

What bands played up there? Yeah, I'll tell you what bands played up there. Well, I do know Lou Armstrong played up there once. I remember Louie played up there once. After he went away and got so famous, he's played up there since he's been famous. But now I'm trying to think of the other guys that played up there. This fellow Peter William, he played up there. He's a drummer, Dixieland musician. Peter William and his band played up there. Drums, piano, bass, violin, tenor, banjo. This fellow Guy E, the one who got killed at the Cadillac out here at the Alpaville and Burgundy there. You know about Guy E getting killed, banjo player. Well, he was playing up there at that time. I remember all the numbers was new at that time. I mean, the old numbers, I remember the numbers that they played, you know, Junk Man, Rag, played Winter Night, and they played the, anybody seen My Kitty? Do you know that? Yeah, I know that. Can you play it for me? Yeah.
